question: What is the primary objective of patient isolation in healthcare facilities?
explanation: Isolation creates a physical barrier to stop pathogens from spreading to other patients and staff, effectively breaking the chain of infection. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why are immunocompromised patients placed in protective isolation?

options.A: To monitor their vital signs every hour
options.B: To make their medication administration easier
options.C: To shield them from external infections
options.D: To prevent them from talking to visitors

explanation: Immunocompromised patients lack strong immune systems, so protective isolation shields them from catching germs present in the hospital environment. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h1)

question: Who must standard precautions be applied to during routine clinical care?

options.B: Patients admitted to the surgical ward

explanation: Standard precautions apply universally to all patients because infection status is not always known upon admission. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h2)

question: When should transmission-based precautions be initiated for a hospitalized patient?

options.A: At the time of the patient's discharge
options.B: During routine morning vital sign checks
options.C: When an infection is suspected or confirmed
options.D: Only after laboratory cultures return positive

explanation: Transmission-based precautions are added to standard precautions the moment a specific transmissible pathogen is suspected or confirmed. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h2)

question: What personal protective equipment is required for airborne precautions?
explanation: Airborne precautions require specialized respiratory protection like an N95 mask to filter out microscopic droplet nuclei. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which infection route requires the use of contact precautions?

options.A: Direct touching of the patient or their environment
options.B: Inhalation of tiny particles floating in the air
options.D: Bites from infected mosquitoes and vectors

explanation: Contact precautions prevent the spread of germs transferred by touching either the infected person or contaminated surfaces nearby. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h3)

question: When should a nurse don personal protective equipment for an isolated patient?

options.A: While standing at the nurses' station

explanation: PPE must be put on prior to room entry to ensure complete protection against environmental pathogens from the very start. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h4)

question: What action must a nurse take immediately after removing personal protective equipment?

options.B: Put on a second pair of gloves
options.D: Document the procedure in the chart

explanation: Hand hygiene is performed immediately after removing PPE to eliminate any pathogens that may have transferred to the hands during doffing. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h4)

question: What type of pressure is maintained in an airborne infection isolation room?
explanation: Negative pressure rooms pull air inward when doors open, preventing infectious aerosols from drifting out into hospital hallways. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is a protective environment room designed with positive air pressure?

options.A: To make the electronic monitor alarms louder
options.B: To remove unpleasant odors from the bathroom
options.C: To stop outside contaminated air from entering
options.D: To cool the room down faster for staff comfort

explanation: Positive pressure pushes air outward, ensuring that unfiltered hallway air and dust do not enter the room of a vulnerable patient. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h5)

question: What common psychological effect is frequently experienced by isolated patients?
explanation: Restricted human contact and confinement can cause loneliness, sensory deprivation, and high levels of anxiety in patients. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h6)

question: How can a nurse best support the mental well-being of an isolated patient?

options.A: Keep the room doors locked at all times
options.B: Limit all nursing visits to prevent staff fatigue
options.C: Remove all personal belongings from the bedside
options.D: Communicate frequently and explain the reasons for isolation

explanation: Regular communication and clear explanations reduce feelings of abandonment and help the patient understand that isolation is for safety. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h6)
